entries.sense_en: poor country people; here, a joking word for the villagers
entries.sense_ko: 시골 농민층, 촌사람들(여기서는 마을 사람들을 놀리는 말)

synonyms.nuance: Neutral: people who live in a village; no suggestion of low class.
synonyms.example: the villagers gathered in the square

synonyms.nuance: Friendly, everyday phrase for people who live outside towns.
Literary and often mocking: simple, unsophisticated country people.

entries.sense_en: the love of parents for their children
entries.sense_ko: 자식 사랑, 부모의 자식에 대한 애정

synonyms.nuance: Plain, everyday wording for the same idea; the story’s word is a deliberately showy joke.
Strong loyalty and love toward anyone or anything, not only children.
Milder, gentler liking; philoprogenitiveness is a strong, instinctive drive.

entries.sense_en: lazy and without energy or interest

synonyms.nuance: Blunt everyday word: unwilling to work. Lackadaisical stresses a lack of care or effort.
Effort is made, but without real enthusiasm.
Tired and without energy, often from weakness or boredom.

entries.sense_en: a long, angry speech or piece of writing attacking someone

synonyms.nuance: A loud, angry outburst of speech; usually spoken and shorter than a diatribe.
Informal: angry, rambling talk; can be comic.
Milder: a long talk that scolds or teaches.

entries.sense_en: a local police officer with limited powers, especially in a small town

synonyms.nuance: Standard modern term for any member of the police.
synonyms.example: a police officer at the door

synonyms.nuance: In the US, an elected county law officer; a constable serves a smaller area or court.
Informal slang, sometimes rude.

entries.sense_en: to succeed in doing something difficult or risky

synonyms.nuance: Neutral: do a planned task; says nothing about difficulty.
Succeed despite difficulty, but with less sense of a bold or tricky feat.
Formal: complete something impressive; no sense of a trick or risk.

entries.sense_en: a loan for buying land or a house, which the lender can take back if unpaid

synonyms.nuance: Everyday phrase for a loan used to buy a house.
Legal term: a claim on property until a debt is paid; broader than a mortgage.
Any money owed; a mortgage is a specific debt secured by property.

entries.sense_en: a person who takes property from someone who has not repaid a loan

synonyms.nuance: Someone who takes back an item, such as a car, when payments stop.
Anyone who lends money for interest; does not suggest taking property.
Neutral: a person or bank owed money.

entries.sense_en: a thick patch of bushes and small trees

synonyms.nuance: The usual word for a dense mass of bushes or small trees.
Low plants under tall trees, not a separate clump.
A small group of trees, not thick bushes.

entries.tip_ko: ‘멈추는 장치’ 뜻의 brake와 같은 철자·발음이지만 여기서는 덤불이다.

entries.sense_en: a boxer of medium weight; here, a fierce, hard-hitting fighter
entries.sense_ko: 웰터급 권투 선수(여기서는 사납게 싸우는 사람)

synonyms.nuance: A lighter boxing class; in general use it means unimportant, so do not confuse it.
The heaviest class; also means a very important person.
Older word for any professional boxer.

entries.sense_en: gave someone a name, as a joke

synonyms.nuance: Give a casual, often teasing name; christen sounds more ceremonial.
Informal: give a name or title, often a humorous one.
synonyms.example: the press dubbed her the Iron Lady

synonyms.nuance: Plain, general word.

entries.sense_en: cooked over an open fire or under direct heat

synonyms.nuance: Cook on a rack over heat; the everyday word in British and American English.
Cook in an oven with dry heat, usually for a longer time.
Cook outdoors, often slowly, with smoke or sauce.

entries.sense_en: annoying and troublesome

synonyms.nuance: General word for anything that irritates you.
Slightly stronger and more formal; makes you feel bothered or angry.
Causes small trouble or inconvenience rather than real anger.

entries.sense_en: to stretch one’s neck to look around; to stare curiously

synonyms.nuance: The full slang form: to stare at something, often an accident, out of curiosity.
Look closely, often because it is hard to see.
Stare rudely with an open mouth.

entries.sense_en: quiet and secret so as not to be noticed

synonyms.nuance: Informal and negative: dishonest or tricky.
Nervous and guilty, like someone afraid of being caught.
Simply hidden from others; says nothing about quiet movement.

entries.sense_en: shouting in a loud, high, harsh voice

synonyms.nuance: A sudden, sharp cry, often from fear or excitement.
The most general loud, high cry, from fear, pain or anger.
Loud shout, usually not high-pitched.

entries.sense_en: to make a sound or give off something

synonyms.nuance: Everyday phrase, mostly for smells, heat or light.
Say or make a sound with the voice; emit also fits machines and light.
Let something go or pour out, often gas or energy.

entries.sense_en: without any self-control; unable to stop

synonyms.nuance: The usual modern word: in a way that cannot be stopped.
Emphasizes being unable to do anything about it.
Emphasizes energy or excitement, not lack of self-control.

entries.tip_ko: 오늘날 incontinent는 주로 ‘요실금’ 뜻으로 쓰이므로, 옛 뜻(자제 못 함)임에 주의.

entries.sense_en: in a hard-working, busy way

synonyms.nuance: With careful, steady effort; suggests attention to detail.
Stresses being occupied, not necessarily effective.
Plain and everyday, with no flavor of careful steady work.

entries.sense_en: to love someone so much that you spoil them

synonyms.nuance: Love very deeply; no sense of being foolish or spoiling.
Give too much, harming character; dote is about love, spoil about the result.
Hold dear and take care of; more formal and gentle.

entries.tip_ko: 보통 dote on + 사람 형태로 쓴다.

entries.sense_en: to look over an area to gather information, especially before an action

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word: go ahead to look for information or danger.
Look at or measure a whole area carefully, not necessarily in secret.
Slang: look over a place before robbing it.

entries.tip_ko: 프랑스어에서 온 단어로 ‘리커노이터’처럼 발음하며, 강세는 -noi- 에 있다.

entries.sense_en: next to or touching; nearby

synonyms.nuance: Next to something, though not always touching; the common word in normal writing.
Everyday word for things or places right beside each other.
Sharing a wall or border.

entries.sense_en: farmers who own their own small farms

synonyms.nuance: Plain word for anyone who farms; yeomanry stresses owning the land.
Modern British word for people who own small pieces of farmland.
Poor rural workers, often without land of their own.

entries.sense_en: a tool with a long curved blade for cutting grass or grain

synonyms.nuance: A smaller, short-handled curved blade used with one hand.
A garden tool with a flat blade for breaking soil, not cutting.
A long fork for lifting hay, listed with the scythe in the story.

entries.sense_en: cowardly and cruel; wicked in a sneaky way

synonyms.nuance: Lacking courage; does not add cruelty or dishonesty.
Deserving hatred or contempt; general, not specifically sneaky.
Like a storybook villain; wicked and evil.

entries.sense_en: here and there; in all directions

synonyms.nuance: The plain, modern way to say it.
Movement in two directions again and again, not scattered around.
Informal: everywhere, often in a messy way.

entries.sense_en: news; a report of events

synonyms.nuance: The normal modern word; tidings is old-fashioned or poetic.
Informal: a message or report, often from a person.
More official: a formal account of what happened.

entries.sense_en: of the woods; peaceful and countryside-like

synonyms.nuance: Plain word: covered with trees.
Everyday adjective or noun for forest areas.
Of the countryside in general, not necessarily forest.

entries.sense_en: sleepy and quiet; nearly asleep

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for a person who feels sleepy.
Simplest word; can describe people and quiet places.
Slow and low in energy, not necessarily from sleep.

entries.sense_en: to wake up after being knocked out; also, to start thinking sensibly again

synonyms.nuance: Wake up from fainting or being knocked out; says nothing about sense.
synonyms.example: she came to in the ambulance

synonyms.nuance: Stop being asleep or, figuratively, become aware of reality.
Informal: suddenly stop a foolish or sad state of mind.
synonyms.example: snap out of it and get to work

entries.tip_ko: ‘생각이 바르게 돌아오다’라는 뜻으로도, ‘의식이 돌아오다’라는 뜻으로도 쓰인다.

entries.sense_en: in a silent, bad-tempered way

synonyms.nuance: Informal: in a mildly bad-tempered, complaining way.
With changing, gloomy feelings.
With anger about something felt to be unfair.

entries.sense_en: commanding, expecting to be obeyed without question

synonyms.nuance: Informal and negative: likes giving orders.
Shows natural authority, often admired.
Tries to control others in an unpleasant way.

entries.sense_en: to criticize something publicly as bad or wrong

synonyms.nuance: Strong, formal blame, often on moral grounds.
Publicly and strongly accuse or condemn.
Make something seem small or unimportant.

entries.sense_en: agreed to a request or demand

synonyms.nuance: Plain, everyday word for having the same view or saying yes.
Informal; means yielding after resisting.
Give formal permission.

entries.tip_ko: ‘액시드’처럼 읽으며, 강세는 두 번째 음절(-cede)에 있다.

entries.sense_en: to do what a rule or demand requires

synonyms.nuance: Do what a person in authority orders; comply is more formal and for rules.
Follow a standard or the behavior of a group.
Accept and follow a rule or decision.

entries.sense_en: betraying someone who trusts you; tricking the other side

synonyms.nuance: The general act of being disloyal to someone.
Lying or tricking; not necessarily breaking trust.
Betraying one’s own country; a legal crime.

entries.sense_en: secretly, so that no one would notice

synonyms.nuance: Simple and general: hidden from others.
Formal; often about spying or official secrets.
In a nervous, guilty manner.

entries.sense_en: a country person seen as simple and unsophisticated

synonyms.nuance: Mocking word for a clumsy, unsophisticated country person.
American slang, insulting: an ignorant person from the country.
Literary and less insulting: a simple country person.

entries.tip_ko: 놀리는 말이므로 실생활에서는 쓰지 않는 것이 좋다.

entries.sense_en: an open, grassy space in a forest

synonyms.nuance: The everyday word for an open space in woods; glade sounds more poetic.
A grassy field, not necessarily inside a forest.
A small group of trees, the opposite of an open space.

entries.sense_en: a person who deserts their side or group

synonyms.nuance: Someone who betrays their country or friends; stronger and more serious.
A soldier who runs away from the army.
Someone who changes sides for personal gain.

entries.sense_en: a natural tendency to behave in a certain way

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for a habit or likelihood.
A mild leaning toward something one likes.
Formal; often for a habit that is slightly bad.

entries.sense_en: to bring under control by force; here Bill mixes it up with ‘subjected to’ (made to suffer)
entries.sense_ko: 굴복시키다(여기서는 subjected to ‘~을 당하다’를 잘못 쓴 말)

synonyms.nuance: Bring under control, often by force or by calming.
Defeat and take over, usually a land or an enemy.
Make someone go through something unpleasant; the phrase Bill really means.

entries.tip_ko: subjugate(정복하다)를 subject(~을 당하게 하다)와 혼동한 말실수다.

entries.sense_en: robbery and damage; plundering

synonyms.nuance: Taking goods by force, especially in war.
Stealing during a riot or disaster.
The everyday word for stealing with force or threat.

entries.sense_en: a dishonest way of making money; a racket

synonyms.nuance: Informal: an organized dishonest scheme for making money.
A trick to cheat people out of money.
Dishonest use of power, especially by officials, for money.

entries.tip_ko: 영국 영어에서 graft는 ‘힘든 일’이라는 뜻으로도 쓰이니 문맥에 주의.

entries.sense_en: having a taste that is pleasant enough to eat

synonyms.nuance: Clearly good-tasting; palatable only means acceptable.
Safe to eat, without saying whether it tastes good.
Looks or smells good and makes you want to eat.

entries.sense_en: burned with heat or chemicals to seal a wound

synonyms.nuance: Burn the surface with sudden strong heat.
Clean a wound to kill germs; no burning.
Close something so nothing gets in or out.

entries.sense_en: too great to be put into words

synonyms.nuance: The everyday word; cannot be described.
Cannot be put into words, especially a feeling.
Often means too terrible to talk about.

entries.sense_en: found new strength and courage

synonyms.nuance: Regain control after being upset or frightened.
Become happier; brace up is about finding courage.
synonyms.example: cheer up, it’s not so bad

synonyms.nuance: Suddenly become livelier.

entries.sense_en: a secret plan made to stop someone else’s plan

synonyms.nuance: A neutral, official word for an action taken to stop something.
A hidden device or trick to catch someone.
A secret plan by a group to do something bad.
synonyms.example: a conspiracy to rob the bank

entries.sense_en: to be recommended to; to appeal to

synonyms.nuance: Say that something is good and worth trying.
Say that someone or something is good; commend is more formal.
Be attractive to someone.

entries.tip_ko: commend itself to ~는 ‘~의 마음에 들다’라는 관용적 쓰임이다.

entries.sense_en: written in small, cramped letters that are hard to read

synonyms.nuance: Squeezed into too little space.
Impossible to read.
Written quickly and messily.

entries.sense_en: the main point; the essential meaning

synonyms.nuance: Informal: the general idea, without details.
The most basic quality of something.
Plain and everyday.
synonyms.example: the main point of the talk

entries.sense_en: a person who spends money wastefully; here ironic, since Dorset’s ‘liberal offer’ makes the kidnappers pay him
entries.sense_ko: 돈을 헤프게 쓰는 사람(여기서는 오히려 유괴범에게 돈을 받으려는 도싯을 두고 한 반어)

synonyms.nuance: Informal: someone who spends freely, sometimes admiringly.
synonyms.example: a big spender at the casino

synonyms.nuance: Someone who wastes money or chances.
Literary: reckless with money, from the Bible story of the prodigal son.

entries.sense_en: an old London hospital for mentally ill people; a madhouse

synonyms.nuance: Old-fashioned and rude word for a mental hospital; also a very chaotic place.
Old term for an institution for the mentally ill.
Complete disorder; lowercase bedlam means noisy confusion.

entries.tip_ko: 소문자 bedlam은 ‘아수라장’이라는 뜻의 일반 명사로도 쓰인다.

entries.sense_en: to make someone feel irritated

synonyms.nuance: General word for causing mild irritation.
Slightly stronger and more formal than annoy.
Very strong and informal: annoy someone almost past bearing.

entries.sense_en: an escape, especially after a crime

synonyms.nuance: General: getting away from danger or a place.
Formal: running away, often from the law.
Escape from a prison.

entries.tip_ko: ‘휴가, 짧은 여행’이라는 뜻으로도 쓰인다(a weekend getaway).

entries.sense_en: a loud musical instrument played by steam or air, heard at fairs and on riverboats
entries.sense_ko: 증기로 소리 내는 시끄러운 건반 악기(칼리오페)

synonyms.nuance: The descriptive name for the same instrument.
synonyms.example: a steam organ on the showboat

synonyms.nuance: A general keyboard instrument, often in churches; softer than a calliope.
A single high sound; a calliope has many steam whistles.

entries.sense_en: to hurry and make an effort

synonyms.nuance: Plain everyday command.
synonyms.example: hurry up or we’ll be late

synonyms.nuance: Informal: start moving quickly.
Informal: go faster, especially in a vehicle.

entries.sense_en: running away fast

synonyms.nuance: Plain: leave quickly by running.
Suddenly run toward escape or a goal.
synonyms.example: make a dash for the door

synonyms.nuance: Flee, especially in fear.

entries.sense_en: lightly and quickly

synonyms.nuance: Quick and light on the feet.
With little weight or force.
Fast, without suggesting lightness.
